policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'his hour was come' renders either the aorist or the perfect; the only note is an alternative_rendering on 'unto the end' and decides nothing here.

ASV 'And during supper' places the action inside a supper still in progress, which is the present participle; the aorist would make the supper an accomplished event ('supper being ended/having taken place').

ASV 'put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him' makes Judas the genitive possessor of the heart, which is the reading with Ἰούδα in the genitive; the other readings have nominative Ἰούδας as subject of παραδοῖ, leaving the heart unqualified.

ASV 'the heart of Judas Iscariot' attaches Iscariot to a genitive Judas, which requires genitive Ἰσκαριώτου; nominative Ἰσκαριώτης would agree only with a nominative Ἰούδας subject the ASV does not render.

ASV 'Jesus, knowing that the Father had given' supplies a subject that the English participial clause needs in either case; a translator naming the subject carried over from the context is not evidence the Greek printed ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
ASV 'had given' is an English pluperfect inside the ὅτι clause and renders the aorist and the perfect alike.
ASV begins a new sentence 'He saith unto him' with no connective, but English routinely drops καί at a sentence break, so the absence does not settle the reading.
ASV 'He saith unto him' needs a subject pronoun in English whether or not ἐκεῖνος stands in the Greek.
The two readings differ only in the position of μου; ASV 'wash my feet' is the only possible English for both.
Word order of 'Jesus' and 'him' with the article; ASV 'Jesus answered him' renders both alike.
A bare article before the participle, invisible in ASV 'He that is bathed'; the mapped textual_variant note concerns the omission of 'save, and his feet', not this article.
Word order within οὐκ ἔχει χρείαν; ASV 'needeth not' renders both.

ASV 'needeth not save to wash his feet' fits both εἰ μή and the exceptive ἤ, which carries the same 'except' sense after a negated need; the mapped note reports an omission of the whole phrase, which is not among these candidates.
Recitative ὅτι before direct speech; ASV 'said he, Ye are not all clean' leaves it untranslated either way.
ASV 'and taken his garments' needs a coordinating 'and' between English clauses regardless of whether καί stands in the Greek.
ASV 'when he had washed their feet, and taken his garments, and sat down again, he said' reads equally as the finite chain inside the ὅτε clause or as the participle ἀναπεσών resumed by εἶπεν.
ASV 'I know whom I have chosen' renders the indirect interrogative τίνας and the relative οὕς identically.
ASV text reads 'He that eateth my bread', and the mapped textual_variant note assigns 'his bread with me' — the μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ reading — to other authorities, so the text rendered is μου.
ASV 'that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe' does not distinguish aorist from present subjunctive, and the English placement of the temporal clause is free of the Greek order.
ἄν and ἐάν are alternate spellings of the indefinite particle; ASV 'whomsoever I send' renders both.
Article before Ἰησοῦς, with no reflex in ASV 'When Jesus had thus said'.
ASV 'The disciples looked one on another' renders no connective, but an unrendered οὖν is ordinary English practice and does not exclude the reading that prints it.
ASV 'There was at the table reclining' carries no connective, which neither requires nor excludes an added δέ.
Partitive ἐκ with the genitive versus the bare genitive; ASV 'one of his disciples' is the same English for both.

ASV gives direct speech, 'and saith unto him, Tell us who it is', which renders καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰπὲ τίς ἐστιν; the base reading is indirect ('to inquire who it might be') and has no imperative for 'Tell' to translate.
ASV 'He leaning back, as he was, on Jesus' breast' renders ἀναπεσών and excludes ἐπιπεσών ('falling upon'), but the presence or absence of οὖν leaves the remaining two readings open.
ASV 'Jesus therefore answereth' renders an inferential connective at this verb, which only the reading with οὖν supplies.
ASV 'for whom I shall dip the sop, and give it him' makes 'dip' a finite future coordinate with 'give'; the aorist participle βάψας would be subordinate ('having dipped').
ASV 'and give it him' renders a second coordinated future with an explicit dative pronoun, matching καὶ δώσω αὐτῷ rather than the single compound ἐπιδώσω.
ASV 'So when he had dipped the sop' renders the inferential οὖν; the alternative offers καί, which the ASV's 'So' does not translate.
ASV 'he taketh and giveth it to Judas' renders a verb of taking before the giving, which only the reading adding λαμβάνει καί contains.
ASV 'to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot' attaches Iscariot to Simon in the genitive; the dative Ἰσκαριώτῃ would attach it to Judas.
Article before Σατανᾶς, with no reflex in ASV 'then entered Satan into him'.
An added article, invisible in ASV 'because Judas had the bag'.
Article before Ἰησοῦς, with no reflex in ASV 'that Jesus said unto him'.
Word order and the εὐθύς/εὐθέως spelling; ASV 'went out straightway' orders the adverb by English idiom and settles neither.
ASV 'When therefore he was gone out' renders οὖν explicitly; the omission would leave the 'therefore' with nothing behind it.
Article before Ἰησοῦς, with no reflex in ASV 'Jesus saith'.
ASV 13:32 begins 'and God shall glorify him in himself' with no conditional clause; the words 'If God be glorified in him' are absent from the verse, so the ASV rendered the text that omits them.
ASV 'in himself' is compatible with the reflexive ἑαυτῷ and with αὑτῷ/αὐτῷ, which differ only in the editors' accentuation of the same pronoun.
Position of the emphatic ἐγώ; ASV 'Whither I go' renders both orders.
ASV 'Jesus answered, Whither I go' has no indirect object; both other readings add αὐτῷ, which the ASV renders as 'him' where it stands.
ASV 'but thou shalt follow afterwards' has no object pronoun; the alternative adds μοι, which would be rendered 'follow me'.
Article before Πέτρος, with no reflex in ASV 'Peter saith unto him'.
Aorist versus present infinitive after δύναμαι; ASV 'why cannot I follow thee' renders both.
ASV 'Jesus answereth' is the present tense and carries no indirect object; the alternative is aorist ἀπεκρίθη with αὐτῷ, which would give 'Jesus answered him'.
Simple and compound forms of the verb of denial; ASV 'till thou hast denied me thrice' renders both.
